problems.quote:
Called after `applyAngerTime` instead of before it, that random 400–799 ticks would overwrite the
configured `anger_duration` every single time.
problems.issue: The tick range is wrong, and the page contradicts its own quote three lines above. `TimeUtil.rangeOfSeconds(20, 39)` is `UniformInt.of(minInclusive * 20, maxInclusive * 20)` = `UniformInt.of(400, 780)` (build/neoForm/.../net/minecraft/util/TimeUtil.java), and `UniformInt.sample` is `Mth.randomBetweenInclusive(random, min, max)`, i.e. inclusive of 780. 799 would require rangeOfSeconds(20, 39.95).
problems.correction: that random 400–780 ticks would overwrite the configured `anger_duration` every single time.

problems.quote:
followed by up to 14 caller frames with the module's own class and everything under
`net.geraldhofbauer.vanillaplusadditions.mixin` filtered out, so the first frame printed is the
foreign caller.
problems.issue: The conclusion is false. Mixin merges an `@Inject` handler into the *target* class, so the stack frames for `PlayerTeleportDebugMixin` are reported as `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer.vpaLogTeleport` and `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer.teleportTo` — neither starts with `net.geraldhofbauer.vanillaplusadditions.mixin`, so that filter branch never fires for this hook. Only the `HostileEndermenModule.logPlayerTeleport` frame is actually removed, and the first two printed frames are the two ServerPlayer ones; the foreign caller is the third.
problems.correction: …with the module's own class filtered out. The first two frames printed are Mixin's merged `ServerPlayer.vpaLogTeleport` and `ServerPlayer.teleportTo`; the foreign caller follows them. (The mixin-package filter in the code is dead for this hook, because merged handlers carry the target class's name.)

problems.quote:
`ServerPlayer#teleportTo(double, double, double)` is where every in-dimension displacement of a
player ends up, `LivingEntity.randomTeleport` included
problems.issue: Overstated, and the caveat two paragraphs later mislabels the other overload. ServerPlayer has two `teleportTo(ServerLevel, …)` methods (ServerPlayer.java:1535 and :1806) and both handle the same-dimension case themselves — `if (newLevel == this.level()) { this.connection.teleport(x, y, z, yaw, pitch); }` — without ever touching `teleportTo(DDD)`. That is the path `/tp` (TeleportCommand) and plenty of mod teleports take, so a same-dimension displacement can bypass the hook entirely. The module's own javadoc is narrower and says "Every mod-side player displacement".
problems.correction: `ServerPlayer#teleportTo(double, double, double)` is where `LivingEntity.randomTeleport` lands — chorus fruit, ender pearls and both mods above route through it. It is not a universal hook: the `teleportTo(ServerLevel, …)` overloads handle same-dimension teleports too (that is what `/tp` uses) and are not hooked.

problems.quote:
`HurtByTargetGoal` sits at target-selector priority 2 and
works off the enderman's 64-block follow range, not our 16
problems.issue: Priority 2 is right (EnderMan.java:105), but the range claim is not. `HurtByTargetGoal.canUse` tests with `HURT_BY_TARGETING = TargetingConditions.forCombat().ignoreLineOfSight().ignoreInvisibilityTesting()`, which never calls `.range(...)`; `TargetingConditions.test` only applies a distance check `if (this.range > 0.0)`, so acquisition through the revenge memory is range-unbounded. The 64-block follow range appears only in `TargetGoal.canContinueToUse`. The page's conclusion (that 16 blocks is not the bound) still holds.
problems.correction: `HurtByTargetGoal` sits at target-selector priority 2 and is not bounded by our 16 at all — its `HURT_BY_TARGETING` conditions set no range, and only `TargetGoal.canContinueToUse` applies the enderman's 64-block follow range.

problems.quote: [JAVA SOURCE, NOT THE DOC — HostileEndermenConfig.java:86] LOGGER.debug("  - Suppress teleport attack: {}", suppressTeleportAttack.get());
problems.issue: Genuine latent NPE: the enclosing guard is `if (detectionRange != null && angerDuration != null && respectCarvedPumpkin != null)`, which does not cover `suppressTeleportAttack`. If that field were ever null while the other three are not, `onConfigLoad` throws. The doc already flags the asymmetry and calls it harmless, which is true today because all six values are built in the same `buildModuleSpecificConfig` call — reporting it here only as the requested Java note.
problems.correction: Add `suppressTeleportAttack != null` to the guard (or use the accessor `suppressTeleportAttack()` which already null-checks).

problems.quote: [JAVA SOURCE, NOT THE DOC — HostileEndermenModule.java:40] /** Static handle for the Enderman Overhaul compat mixin, which has no module instance. */
problems.issue: Wrong/outdated comment: the static `instance` field is read by all three mixin entry points — `suppressTeleportAttack` (Enderman Overhaul), `suppressAntiCheeseTeleport` (EnhancedAI) and `logPlayerTeleport` (the ServerPlayer diagnostics) — not just the Enderman Overhaul one.
problems.correction: "Static handle for the three compat/diagnostic mixins, which have no module instance."

problems.issue: Effectively dead code. The only mixin that reaches `logPlayerTeleport` is `PlayerTeleportDebugMixin`, whose `@Inject` handler Mixin merges into `net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer`; stack frames therefore report the ServerPlayer class name and never match this prefix. The intended effect (log opens at the foreign caller) is not achieved — every log line starts with two ServerPlayer frames, eating 2 of the 14 slots.
problems.correction: Filter the merged frames by method name (`vpaLogTeleport`) or skip the first N frames, if opening at the foreign caller is the goal.

problems.quote: [JAVA SOURCE, NOT THE DOC — HostileEndermenModule.java:255] return player.distanceToSqr(enderman) <= range * range;
problems.issue: Minor inconsistency between the two range measurements. `findNearestTarget` calls `level().getNearestPlayer(getX(), getEyeY(), getZ(), range, …)`, which measures from the enderman's *eye*; `isInRange` measures entity-centre to entity-centre. At the boundary the two disagree by up to the enderman's eye height (~2.55 blocks), so a player right at `detection_range` can be "still in range" for the keep-current-victim branch but not findable as the nearest target on the next pass, or vice versa. Benign at the default 16, but it is an inconsistency, not a deliberate hysteresis.
problems.correction: Use the same reference point in both checks (either both eye-based or both position-based).
